title: Run at startup only works for a single user account
summary: Startup task names collide for local and domain accounts sharing the same username.

judgment.rationale: The report describes an account-name collision consistent with the task-name construction; the scenario has not been reproduced in this pass.
evidence: On 0.69.0 the reporter describes two admin accounts sharing a username across local and domain authorities; the last to toggle startup owns the single task.
The reporter confirmed the behavior again in November 2024.
In src/runner/auto_start_helper.cpp create, delete and active-check build the task name from USERNAME alone; creation separately uses USERDOMAIN and USERNAME for the trigger principal.
Open PR https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/pull/51687 also changes autorun task handling for a different report; coordinate rather than duplicate its work.
judgment.recommended_action: Reproduce the collision and coordinate any account-qualified task naming proposal with the active autorun work.

fix_assessment.rationale: Account-specific identification is a plausible direction; coordination with open PR #51687 and safe legacy migration are prerequisites.

proposed_fixes.title: Investigate account-unique startup task identifiers
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Hypothesis: USERNAME-only task names collide for distinct local and domain principals sharing the same name.
plan: Reproduce with two accounts sharing the same account name but different authorities; establish existing task principal and trigger behavior.
Coordinate with #51687, then design a stable account-unique task identifier consistently across create, query and delete operations.
Define safe handling for legacy task names by verifying task ownership before migrating or deleting; never remove another principal’s task.
Add focused coverage for distinct same-name principals, enabling/disabling one without affecting the other, and legacy migration.
verification: Test both account logons and repeated toggles without overwriting the other principal or losing startup.
Test upgrades from a legacy task and verify unrelated tasks and ACLs remain unchanged.

confidence.rationale: Current naming uses only USERNAME and matches the reported setup, but current behavior and safe migration are unverified and adjacent autorun work is active.

issue_context.summary: Startup task names collide for local and domain accounts sharing the same username.
known_information: On 0.69.0 the reporter describes two admin accounts sharing a username across local and domain authorities; the last to toggle startup owns the single task.
The reporter confirmed the behavior again in November 2024.
inferences: A same-name collision is consistent with the username-only task identifier; this is not proof of all reported task mutations.
initial_investigation: Inspected src/runner/auto_start_helper.cpp creation, deletion and active-task lookup, including USERNAME-only task naming and the domain-qualified trigger identity.
Reviewed current public discussion, no assignee and relevant open autorun PR #51687; that PR addresses task recreation rather than explicitly claiming this collision.
issue_context.analysis: The reported accounts are distinguishable by principal but their task identifiers may collide. Migration must not delete or adopt another user’s task, and must be coordinated with existing task-validation work.

information_gaps.information: Whether same-name local and domain accounts still overwrite or lose each other’s task on a current build.
information_gaps.why_needed: Confirms the collision and migration behavior before selecting a change.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Maintainer tests two distinct accounts with the same username and inspects task names, principals and logon triggers after each toggle.

actions.label: Approve investigation of account-unique startup tasks

reproduce.title: Compare distinct same-name account startup tasks
reproduce.version_requirement: Use a current PowerToys build; compare the historical 0.69 report as needed.
prerequisites: Use a test machine with two authorized administrator accounts, one local and one domain account, sharing the same username.
setup: Record existing PowerToys scheduled tasks and preserve any unrelated tasks.
steps: 1. Sign in as the first account, enable Run at startup, sign out and verify startup on its next login.
2. Repeat as the second account, then inspect the PowerToys task names, principals and logon triggers.
3. Sign back in as the first account and verify startup; toggle startup for one account and verify the other remains intact.
reproduce.expected_result: Both distinct principals retain their own startup task and disabling one does not alter the other.
